title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Notable Recent Papers — 2026-11-19
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred relevance-ranked selection from an incomplete biomedical preprint corpus, not a popularity ranking; bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the wider clinical literature are not covered.

sections.title: Headline
sections.text: Latest batch announced Thursday, 19 November 2026; 8 notable papers from the 18 November submission date. The strongest patterns are cross-modal translation into scalable signals, predictive models of cellular dynamics, and better interpretation of molecular and imaging measurements. Agenda: examine what is genuinely measured versus predicted, then note where external validation is still needed. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred, relevance-ranked selection from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
sections.abstract: MyoECG transfers cardiac MRI phenotype information into ECG representations; the authors report cardiomyopathy AUROCs of 0.800–0.974 across seven datasets and improved reader performance in a six-cardiologist study.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim CMR-guided training can transfer structural and functional information into ECG-only cardiomyopathy detection; in their retrospective reader study, assistance improved mean sensitivity and specificity.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective evidence; the paper reports limited positive predictive value in low-prevalence settings and calls for prospective evaluation of calibration, false-positive burden, clinical decisions, resource use, and outcomes. The authors do not position it as a standalone diagnostic test.

sections.title: SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement
sections.abstract: SCOPE uses shared RNA–protein priors to predict single-cell molecular profiles from H&E images, reporting improvements over baselines across 16 organs and two external protein cohorts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim that gene–protein correspondence and biomarker priors let a shared model transfer information across separately measured RNA and protein modalities, including to markers without direct H&E supervision.
sections.unique_caveat: These are image-based predictions, not direct molecular measurements. The authors note that RNA and protein assays came from separate sections rather than paired measurements on the same section; external protein validation involved two cohorts.

sections.title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction
sections.abstract: STORM predicts protein–small-molecule binding affinity by transferring information from experimentally measured reference molecules, without requiring protein–ligand structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report comparable or better affinity-prediction accuracy than Boltz-2 on their evaluation datasets and over five orders of magnitude faster inference and training in their comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The model does not use structural or biophysical signals and depends on historical affinity data and reference-molecule similarity. Dataset split design and performance on genuinely novel targets or scaffolds matter; the preprint does not establish experimental or drug-discovery utility.

sections.title: MitoWorld: A Stochastic World Model of the Single-Cell Cycle under Genetic Perturbation
sections.abstract: MitoWorld models individual cell-image trajectories and division timing after genetic perturbation; on 325 held-out MitoCheck tracks across 17 knockdowns and a control, it reports improved video metrics and calibrated prediction intervals.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim a stochastic generative model can jointly forecast cell appearance and division hazard, with lower FID and JEDi scores than their strongest baselines on the held-out tracks.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is computational and confined to the MitoCheck dataset; generated trajectories and hazard estimates are not direct evidence that predicted perturbation effects will generalize to new cell types or experimental settings.

sections.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
sections.abstract: HORIZON learns spatial transcriptomic tissue dynamics while factoring out shared rotation and translation; the authors report improved reconstruction and held-out-stage interpolation on four spatial transcriptomics time courses.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim horizontal flow matching removes rigid-frame motion from inferred tissue dynamics and enables continuous tissue generation from an initial snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are computational comparisons on four time courses plus simulated alignment tests. Reconstructed dynamics are not direct cell tracking or causal evidence, and broader datasets and experimental settings are needed to assess transfer.

sections.title: Unmyelinated axons alter the biological interpretation of MRI biomarkers of demyelination
sections.abstract: A mouse-model study combining diffusion and relaxation MRI with electron microscopy finds that unmyelinated axons materially affect white-matter MRI metrics commonly interpreted as measures of myelinated fibers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim axonal-water-fraction estimates at short diffusion times reflect total intra-axonal space, and that g-ratio estimates align with EM only when myelinated and unmyelinated axons are both included.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is from a mouse model and does not establish performance or interpretation in human patients. MRI-derived measures and automated EM segmentation remain dependent on acquisition and analysis assumptions.

sections.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
sections.abstract: A structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array reproduces previously reported CheW-dependent response changes and predicts how CheW abundance and placement shape signaling dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors attribute sharper signaling responses to CheW-mediated effective coupling between core units and predict a transition from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations as CheW abundance changes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model, not a new experimental demonstration. CheW states and couplings are indirectly constrained, and the predicted oscillations and assembly effects require direct tests such as single-cell FRET across CheW levels.

sections.title: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data
sections.abstract: LRCBench compares reference-free long-read sequencing compressors across 35 methods and 16 real-world Oxford Nanopore and PacBio datasets, assessing compression, speed, memory, and robustness.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that CoLoRd gave the best overall compression ratios in their tests, while other tools traded off speed, memory use, and robustness.
sections.unique_caveat: Learning-based compressors were evaluated on only six MinION datasets because of computational cost; results depend on the sampled technologies, data, and benchmark settings and are not a biological finding.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Cross-modal translation is present in MyoECG and SCOPE; biological dynamics are modeled in HORIZON, MitoWorld, and the CheW study; MRI/EM interpretation and long-read compression are represented by the MRI/EM study and LRCBench. These papers do not establish a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Prospectively evaluate MyoECG calibration and clinical effects; validate SCOPE against matched same-section RNA/protein assays; test STORM on held-out targets and prospective binding assays; measure CheW predictions with single-cell FRET and investigate MRI/axon interpretation beyond the cuprizone mouse model.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The batch is notable for cross-modal methods and measurement reinterpretation, but it does not establish a popularity surge; validation ranges from retrospective datasets and mouse experiments to computational benchmarks.
